items.subject: Daily pipeline commit REFUSED - 2026-09-09
evidence: capture-run-ad-2026-09-09.log:63-67 (07:02:36 rc=1) and capture-run-daily-2026-09-09.log:646-653 (08:35:06 rc=1) both end 'commit: REFUSED (git exit 1) - a hook or git itself rejected this commit': BOTH scheduled runs were refused, not one, and neither transcript carries a single line of the hook's diagnosis - the log goes straight from 'prompt-sync rc=0' to 'commit: REFUSED'.

REPRODUCED in a scratch index (GIT_INDEX_FILE under the scratchpad, git read-tree HEAD, then exactly capture-run's add set from lib\bot-paths.ps1): the ad shape stages 118 paths (91 under grocery/out, 16 under graph/identity, the ledgers), the daily shape 134 (the same plus 16 served paths). In BOTH, the hook's first exit fires: ops\verify-bulk-edit.ps1 -Staged rc=1 with exactly ONE finding, 'BOM CHANGED grocery/out/json-readers-baseline.json - a read/write pair stripped or added a byte-order mark'. verify-bot-commit-scope rc=0 ('all 118 / 134 staged path(s) are inside lib\bot-paths.ps1'), verify-commodities-gate rc=0 ('not applicable'). The hook itself, run through bash with stderr captured to a file: rc=1, 'pre-commit: BLOCKED. The staged set fails a bulk-edit invariant'.

The file: HEAD (69516845e, 2026-09-05) begins EF BB BF, 160 bytes; the working tree begins 7B 0D 0A, 162 bytes, mtime 2026-09-09 05:45:24, content otherwise identical (generated still 2026-09-05T15:56:28, count 0; the +2 bytes are CRLF vs LF, which git normalises on add). Only grocery\audit-json-readers.ps1:174 names this file, and both of its write paths (:180, :203) use Set-Content -Encoding UTF8, which under PS 5.1 writes a BOM and refreshes 'generated' - neither can produce this file. The only repo files written between 05:43 and 05:48:30 are ops\audit-one-way-actuators.ps1 (05:44:04), this baseline (05:45:24) and grocery\audit-json-readers.ps1 (05:47:41), committed as a45bc1008 at 05:48:02: a content-preserving, BOM-stripping read-then-write-back by that session.

Which reader surfaces are stale, per surface (all read 10:00-10:10 with cache-busting query strings): the Ghost page www.thriftycrew.com/omaha-grocery-prices/ is FRESH ('updated Sep 9', Baby Back Ribs $3.14/lb Sam's = the 08:11 board; publish-deals-page ships to Ghost directly, not through git). feed.thriftycrew.com/smp-feed.json serves generated 2026-09-08T11:40:41 = HEAD:public/smp-feed.json (54326d19e) while the working tree holds 2026-09-09T08:13:19: STALE, and the 583 recipe pages price off it. feed.thriftycrew.com/board.json = HEAD bytes, whose baby-back-ribs chip is Baker's $2.99 from the 09-02 ad that EXPIRED 09-08, while the working-tree chip is Sam's $3.14: STALE and showing an expired sale. The alert's 'the live board and feed are STALE' is wrong for the page and right for the chips and the feed.

Verdict: the refusal is CORRECT at the invariant (a tracked JSON under out\ lost its BOM, exactly the read/write-pair class verify-bulk-edit exists for) and MISATTRIBUTED (the pipeline did not write the file; it stages grocery/out as a whole directory and inherited a session's edit). The hook is not weakened. What was broken is that the artifact a human is sent to read could not say WHY, across five different refusal causes.

surface_fix.what: restore the BOM on the one file the hook named; its content already equals HEAD
surface_fix.exact_change: git -C C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew checkout -- grocery/out/json-readers-baseline.json  (explicit path; working-tree content equals HEAD apart from the BOM and line endings, so nothing is lost). Then re-run the scratch-index reproduction: ops\verify-bulk-edit.ps1 -Staged over the bot's add set must print '0 finding(s)'. FIRST re-read the file's first three bytes: if a session already rewrote it with a BOM, this step is done.

items.root_cause: capture-run.ps1:857-866 runs `git commit` through a stdout-only pipe and reads $LASTEXITCODE; the pre-commit hook writes its ENTIRE diagnosis to stderr (every echo in .git/hooks/pre-commit is >&2, and it discards the checkers' own stderr with 2>/dev/null), and a -WindowStyle Hidden transcript never sees a native child's stderr. Five distinct refusal exits (two missing checkers, a bulk-edit invariant, a scope breach, an unreviewed rule change) plus git's own errors all collapse into one sentence, so a refusal costs a full reproduction instead of a glance; lib\pipeline-commit.ps1:150 (`commit ... | Out-Null`) has the identical blind spot. One level up: the bot stages grocery/out as a whole directory, so any session's edit to any of the roughly 300 tracked entries under out\ becomes the pipeline's refusal on every scheduled run until a human finds the file, and today nothing told the human which file.

root_fix.what: capture the commit's stderr and put it in the transcript and the alert, without 2>&1 and without an EAP=Stop redirect
root_fix.exact_change: add Invoke-GitCaptured -Repo <path> -GitArgs <string[]> to lib\git-blob-lib.ps1 using System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo (FileName git; UseShellExecute $false; RedirectStandardOutput and RedirectStandardError $true; CreateNoWindow $true; the child inherits GIT_INDEX_FILE from the environment exactly as today) returning @{ rc; stdout; stderr }; read stderr via ReadToEndAsync (or BeginErrorReadLine) BEFORE WaitForExit so a long hook output cannot deadlock the pipe. capture-run.ps1:857 and lib\pipeline-commit.ps1:150 call it for the commit; on rc -ne 0 they Write-Output every stderr line prefixed 'commit:hook> ' into the transcript, put the first 20 stderr lines in the REFUSED alert body, and extract the paths named on lines matching 'BOM CHANGED|PARSE FAIL|DEPENDENCY|FROZEN LITERAL|REFUSING|BLOCKED' into one 'files named by the hook:' line so the alert says WHICH FILE. No `2>&1` and no `2>$null` anywhere near it: under PS 5.1 with EAP=Stop the first stderr line becomes a terminating error, the trap capture-run documents three times.

blast_radius.measured_by: every `git ... commit` call site in the estate's committers: grocery/capture-run.ps1:857 and lib/pipeline-commit.ps1:150 (both pipe stdout only); the hook's five refusal exits enumerated from .git/hooks/pre-commit; scratch-index reproduction of both staging shapes (118 and 134 paths). No matching rule changes and no board cell moves.
blast_radius.risk: the helper changes how git's streams are READ, never what is staged or committed; the private-index pattern, the size gate, the resync loop and the push loop are untouched. The one real hazard is reading stderr after WaitForExit (pipe deadlock on a chatty hook) - read it asynchronously.

items.resolution_note: Both scheduled runs were refused by the pre-commit hook's bulk-edit check on ONE file: grocery/out/json-readers-baseline.json lost its BOM in a session's 05:45 rewrite and the bot stages grocery/out wholesale. The hook was right; the log could not say so because the commit step captured no stderr. BOM restored from HEAD; git commit now runs through Invoke-GitCaptured in capture-run and pipeline-commit so a refusal logs the hook's own lines and the alert names the file. The Ghost page was never stale; smp-feed and board.json at the edge were (one build behind, with an expired Baker's chip) and re-ship on this run's rebuild.
items.premise_verified: TRUE, checked four ways. (1) The file: worktree bytes were 7b 0d 0a (no BOM, CRLF, 162 bytes), HEAD blob ef bb bf 7b 0a (BOM, LF, 160 bytes), and with the BOM and CRs stripped both sides hash identically (sha256 7fd65c10786ff7126bbad9f032d9ef327b71c9681e1ef985e4ad70c8476b90fe), so nothing was lost by restoring HEAD. Restored with git checkout -- and proved byte-identity by piping a FRESH git cat-file -p HEAD:grocery/out/json-readers-baseline.json into cmp, never against my own output. (2) Scratch-index reproduction re-run under GIT_INDEX_FILE: the ad shape staged 116 paths and the daily shape 132, and ops\verify-bulk-edit.ps1 -Staged printed "0 finding(s)" with exit 0 on both. (3) Both transcripts confirm the refusal and its silence: capture-run-ad-2026-09-09.log:63 at 07:02:36 and capture-run-daily-2026-09-09.log:646 at 08:35:06 both read "commit: REFUSED (git exit 1)" and neither carries one line of the hook's diagnosis. (4) verify-bulk-edit -SelfTest still exits 0 with its BOM must-fire firing, so the invariant was not weakened to get the commit through.
items.deviation:
THE DISPATCH'S DISCOVERED DEFECT IS A FALSE PREMISE, and no change was made for it. Claim: "capture-run.ps1 cites a lib
ative-lib.ps1 that does not exist." Measured: capture-run.ps1 names 32 distinct .ps1 basenames and 31 resolve. native-lib.ps1 resolves to grocery
ative-lib.ps1, a sibling of capture-run.ps1, and the single mention at :753 is prose provenance rather than a dependency (capture-run calls no Invoke-Native at all). The strings "lib
ative-lib" and "lib/native-lib" do not occur anywhere in the main tree. The one basename that does not resolve is run-daily-local.ps1, retired 2026-08-22 to grocery\archiveetired-2026-08-22\, and all five of its mentions in capture-run.ps1 state outright that it was retired and name where its jobs went, so they are deliberate history and not a stale reference. Editing correct prose to satisfy an unmeasured claim would have been the change nobody measured, so it was recorded instead.

TWO ADDITIONS BEYOND THE PLAN, both forced by the work. (a) The REFUSED alert body said "the live board and feed are STALE", which the plan's own evidence shows was wrong for the Ghost page: publish-deals-page ships to Ghost directly rather than through git, so the page was fresh all morning. The body now names what a refused commit actually strands, public oard.json and public\smp-feed.json, and says the Ghost page is unaffected. (b) The frozen fixture strings in lib\git-blob-lib.ps1 quote the hook's own stderr, which spells grocery/out paths, and ops\audit-cross-module-reach.ps1 counted them as ten NEW cross-module reaches and its ratchet ROSE 133 -> 143. Every one of the ten was mine and every one was fixture text, not a read. The ratchet was NOT raised. That detector had already been refined the same day for the same shape ("AN ENTRY POINT IS NOT A DATA REACH", 2026-09-09) rather than by moving the baseline, and its own line 191 already states the principle ("a detector must never scan itself: its own fixtures are full of the literals it hunts"). Following that precedent, a site whose line carries "# reach-fixture-ok: <reason>" is no longer counted; the marker is opt-in, per line, requires a reason, and no line in the tree carried it when it was added, so the measured 133 is untouched. Four new self-test cases cover it, including a MUST FIRE that an unmarked fixture literal is still counted and a MUST FIRE that the marker does not reach the next line. The audit now reads code=133 base=133, exit 0.

items.subject: Daily chain left served files uncommitted - 2026-09-09
evidence: capture-run.ps1:940 gates the served-dirty block on `if ($shipServed)` alone; $botCommitted (set at :864 from the commit's exit code) is never read by it, and the alert body at :946 hard-codes 'The chain ran, guards passed and the bot commit went out'. On this run the commit was REFUSED - daily log :646, one line above the served-dirty line at :647.

All 16 files in the alert are inside Get-BotServedPaths (Test-BotPathOwned true for 16 of 16: meal-prep/cheapnow-data.js, db/costed.json, db/recipes/cowboy-pork-and-beans-biscuit-bake.json, dinner-data.js, free-rotation.json, ingredient-map.json, pipeline/v2-perserving.json, v2-perserving.prev.json, recipes-db.json, public/board.json, free-dinners.json, price-history.json, share/omaha-drops.png, smp-feed.json, site/tools/cheap-dinners-tool.html, dinner-tonight-tool.html), and the daily-shape staging reproduction stages every one of them. They are dirty because the commit that staged them was refused, not because a writer is missing from the list: the alert's prescribed repair ('Add the writer's output to $servedPaths') would have been inert.

The edge line at :1093 is the same defect from the other end: it prints the literal 'shipServed=false' from the `elseif ($runDownstream)` branch, which is reached whenever `-not ($shipServed -and $pushed)`. On this run shipServed was TRUE (the served-dirty block, gated on it, ran) and $pushed was false; the line names the wrong variable, and Test-EdgeServesPushed printed 'ok' for a check that never happened because it was handed ShipServed=$true with 'n/a' on both sides. The two lines are not two views of one intended behaviour; they are two watchers that both assume the commit landed, one on each side of the REFUSED line that says it did not.

surface_fix.what: nothing to stage; the 16 files ship on this run's rebuild once a95022's BOM restore lets the commit through

items.root_cause: two post-commit watchers read $shipServed as if it implied the commit succeeded. Both were written the day their shape appeared (served-dirty 2026-09-02, edge decision 2026-09-03), both are fixtured only on runs where the commit landed (test-commit-size-gate drives $shipServed true and false and nothing else), and neither has a case where the commit was refused - so a refused commit turns two watchers into two confident wrong diagnoses, one of which prescribes an edit to the wrong file. A guard that manufactures a confident wrong answer is worse than one that stays quiet.

root_fix.what: branch both watchers on the commit outcome and print the predicate they actually evaluated
root_fix.exact_change: (1) initialise `$botCommitted = $false` before the try at :692 (today it is unassigned on the size-gate and no-changes paths). (2) inside the >>> SERVED-DIRTY BLOCK markers, so the lifted fixture still reaches it: `if ($shipServed -and $botCommitted)` keeps today's behaviour; add `elseif ($shipServed -and -not $botCommitted)` that writes 'served-dirty: N tracked served file(s) dirty because the commit was REFUSED - see commit-refused above; this is not a $servedPaths gap and no served-dirty alert is sent' and adds NO failed lane (commit-refused already is one). (3) the edge line :1093 prints the real values 'shipServed=<v> botCommitted=<v> pushed=<v>' with the reason chosen from them, and passes ShipServed ($shipServed -and $botCommitted -and $pushed) to Test-EdgeServesPushed so it returns 'skipped', never 'ok', for a check that did not run. (4) the alert body at :946 stays under the committed branch only, so its 'the bot commit went out' sentence is true whenever it is sent.

blast_radius.measured_by: the two reader sites of $shipServed after the commit stage (capture-run.ps1:940 and :1089-1093) and the one fixture that lifts the block (test-commit-size-gate.ps1:155-208, three cases, none with a refused commit); Get-BotServedPaths checked against all 16 named files. No matching rule and no cell moves.
blast_radius.risk: the block is dot-sourced by the fixture through the markers, so $botCommitted must be read from the caller's scope under that exact name; keep the markers and the `$failed +=` shape or the fixture goes BLIND (exit 3) rather than red

items.freshness: read from capture-run.ps1 at HEAD 1ccdab0fd (the file is not dirty) and the daily log of 08:35:06; the 16-file dirty set was re-read at 10:20 and is unchanged

proof.guard_or_fixture: grocery\test-commit-size-gate.ps1 SERVED-DIRTY lifted block (Run-Served gains a [bool]$committed parameter, default $true) + the EDGE-DECISION pure function Test-EdgeServesPushed
proof.must_fire_case: frozen, built from today's shape: shipServed TRUE, botCommitted FALSE, meal-prep/db/recipes/x.json rewritten - the block must print 'because the commit was REFUSED', must add NO 'served-dirty' lane and must compose NO alert; and Test-EdgeServesPushed handed ShipServed $false for the refused-commit case must return 'skipped', never 'ok'
proof.clean_twin: the existing case shipServed TRUE, botCommitted TRUE, x.json rewritten still fails the lane and composes the alert naming x.json (the watcher still catches the 2026-09-02 shape); shipServed FALSE still stays silent

items.rollback: revert the marker-delimited hunk and the two edge lines; the fixture's new parameter defaults to $true so the existing three cases are byte-for-byte the same assertions
do_not_touch: the >>> SERVED-DIRTY BLOCK <<< markers (the fixture finds the block by them)
lib\bot-paths.ps1 Get-BotServedPaths - nothing is missing from it
the edge byte comparison against HEAD
items.resolution_note: False premise: the 16 'uncommitted served files' were exactly the served set of a REFUSED commit (a95022), all already in Get-BotServedPaths; the served-dirty check never read the commit outcome and its alert hard-coded 'the bot commit went out', and the edge line printed 'shipServed=false' on a run where it was true. Both now branch on $botCommitted and print the predicate they evaluated. No $servedPaths change.
items.premise_verified: TRUE, and the edge half is SHARPER than the plan recorded. capture-run.ps1 gated the served-dirty block on $shipServed alone and its alert body hard-coded "The chain ran, guards passed and the bot commit went out"; both read in source. The daily log has the refusal at :646 and the served-dirty finding at :647, one line apart. All 16 named files are inside Get-BotServedPaths, which I confirmed by measurement rather than by reading the list: the daily-shape scratch staging staged every one of them (132 paths), so the alert's prescribed repair, adding them to $servedPaths, would have been inert. The edge line :1093 did print the literal "(shipServed=false)" while $shipServed was true, AND, not recorded in the plan, Test-EdgeServesPushed RETURNED "ok": it was handed ShipServed=$true with 'n/a' on both sides, so it walked past its skipped arm and compared 'n/a' with 'n/a'. Daily log :648 reads "edge check skipped: ok" - a check that never ran, reporting a pass, which is the could-not-evaluate-as-pass shape.
items.deviation: Three small departures, all additive. (1) $botCommitted is also set TRUE on the "no pipeline changes to commit" path. The plan only asked for the declaration before the try; without this the new elseif would announce a refusal on a run where there was simply nothing to commit, since an unassigned variable is $null and falsey. (2) test-capture-builders.ps1 asserted the served-dirty block was gated on "^if ($shipServed) {", which my change deliberately made stricter, so that assertion was updated to demand BOTH flags. It is strictly stronger than the one it replaces, not weaker, and a second assertion now pins the refused-commit arm. (3) test-auditors.ps1 pinned the test-capture-builders inventory as an exact "SELFTEST: 28/28 pass", so ADDING cases turned it red and printed the passing run's own output as the failure text. It now reads the CAPTURE-BUILDERS-COMPLETE marker and requires failed=0 with cases at or above a floor of 33, which still catches a silently dropped case, cannot be satisfied by a suite that died halfway, and sits higher than the 28 it replaces.

evidence: DONUTS crown: Fareway | 'Clyde's Donuts Donuts, Powdered Lil’ Smiles, Classic' | $3.49 | size '21 ct' | basis per-21-pack | $0.1662/each | type sale (ad_basis ttl 2026-09-09 to 2026-10-09). The arithmetic is right ($3.49 / 21) and the count is Fareway's own, so this is not a parse bug; a 0.57 oz hole is being priced as one donut. The name never says 'holes', so the existing exclude \bholes\b cannot see it.

DONUTS runner-up: Aldi | '36 CT Donut Cups' | $11.25 | 12.6 oz | per-36-pack | $0.3125/each, found_by_term 'ground coffee' in aldi-regular-2026-09-09.json, 0.35 oz per cup, listed beside 'Barissimo ... Donut Store ... Single Serve Cups 0 37 OZ, 12 ct, $4.59': coffee pods. The name carries none of 'coffee', 'k-cup' or 'pod' - the three coffee excludes donuts has - and coffee-pods (index 257) admits only k-cup / coffee pods / coffee cups, so the name falls through to donuts (index 173).

DONUTS rows 3-4: Walmart 'Krispy Kreme® 12-Count Original Glazed® Doughnut Dots' 4.509 oz $4.78 -> $0.3983/each and Baker's 'Krispy Kreme Original Glazed Doughnut Dots' 12 ct $4.79 -> $0.3992/each are holes under another word ('Dots'). Rows 5-6, Family Fare 'Little Debbie Glazed Donut Sticks 6 Ea' 10 oz $3.19 -> $0.5317 and Sam's 'Duchess Mini Frosted Donuts, 3 oz, 12 pk.' $8.32 -> $0.6933 are sticks and 3 oz bags of minis. Not one of the six rows in the cell is a donut. The real donuts in the corpus (Baker's 'Bakery Fresh Glazed Yeast Donuts 12 pk 2.5 oz' $5.00, Family Fare '12 Ct Glazed Yeast Ring Donuts' 20 oz $10.99, Baker's 'Krispy Kreme Original Glazed Doughnuts 12 ct' $14.29) lose to them, and the Fareway and Aldi real donuts (Big Smile 12 oz $3.49, Bake Shop Chocolate Iced Donuts 15 oz $4.49) carry no count, price as one each, and are censored by the 0.08-2 band.

BABY POTATOES: last week (comparison-2026-09-02) Fareway 'Summertime Farms Baby Red Potatoes' $2.99 / 3 lb SALE -> $0.9967/lb (sale-windows.json: sale_start 2026-08-09, sale_end 2026-09-08, refresh_on 2026-09-09; the 30-day TTL for a markdown with no printed end). This week the same row (fareway-regular-2026-09-09.json: as_of 2026-08-09, current_price 2.99, base_price 4.99, marked_down true) prices at its base $4.99 / 3 lb = $1.6633/lb because the TTL expired 09-08 and compare-deals refuses expired ads. +67% is the markdown ending, not a parse: real economics, no code change. Runner-up Baker's 'Private Selection Petite Gold Gourmet Potatoes' $6.00 / 3 lb = $2.00/lb, unchanged week over week.

BABY POTATOES refresh gap, noted and NOT fixed here: rescue-terms-fareway.txt (08:27) says '# baby-potatoes UNTRACEABLE no capture on disk still carries this exact row' - the row has no found_by_term (it arrived through a product link), so the sale-expiry refresh sale-windows scheduled for 2026-09-09 cannot become a search term, and the $4.99 base is a month-old observation. The row has a link_url (products/84386881-baby-red-potatoes), so the Wednesday link check owns re-pricing it; if the developer wants it sooner, add 'baby red potatoes' to the Fareway worklist by hand.

surface_fix.what: exclude the hole-by-other-name products and the coffee pods from donuts (the estate already excludes \bholes\b; this names the aliases that defeat it)
surface_fix.exact_change: donuts (array index 173).exclude += '\bcups?\b', '\blil.{0,5}smiles?\b', '\bdots\b', '\bpop\W{0,2}ems?\b', '\bmunchkins?\b', '\bbites\b'  (the lil-smiles token tolerates the curly apostrophe and its cp1252 mojibake, both of which occur in today's captures). Then audit-match-soundness.ps1 -Accept against the new rules_hash - ops\verify-commodities-gate.ps1 refuses the commit otherwise.

items.root_cause: the estate already decided holes are not donuts (\bholes\b is in the exclude), but the exclude is word-based on the raw name and four sellers name holes without the word (Lil' Smiles, Doughnut Dots, Pop'ems, Munchkins) while one names coffee pods without 'coffee', 'k-cup' or 'pod' ('36 CT Donut Cups'). The per-each basis then divides by whatever count the store printed, so a 0.57 oz hole or a 0.35 oz coffee pod prices as one donut, and the 0.08-2 band censors the real donuts that carry no count. Class: an each-commodity whose stores cannot all express a portion count, populated by exactly the rows that are not the commodity.
items.root_fix_none_because: the six tokens ARE the class fix for 'a seller's naming defeats a word exclude' on this commodity - every hole and pod alias found in a 19,208-name corpus is now named and the artifact's must_stay controls pin what has to keep routing; the remaining class (per-each across holes, minis, sticks and dozens) is a ruling on what Donuts MEANS and is filed under open_questions_for_brad rather than decided by a rule.

THE ROOT FIX AS SPECIFIED WOULD NOT HAVE SILENCED TODAY'S ALERT, and the measurement says why. The plan has both emitters read browser-capture-due-<today>.flag and stay quiet when it names the store. That flag is ONE FILE PER DATE and every run REWRITES it with only its own outstanding set: the 07:02 ad run wrote it naming Baker's (ad log :32, "BROWSER WORK OUTSTANDING: Baker's") and the 08:06 daily run overwrote the same file naming Aldi and Walmart (daily log :591, flag mtime 08:06:39). The per-store worklists are not a substitute either: all seven stores have a capture-<store>-2026-09-09.json, including the three that WERE driven, so gating on them would silence every store permanently.

A flag written before this change has no `owned` map and still confers ownership from its mtime, so nothing goes blind in the meantime. open_questions_for_brad.question: Donuts is priced per each, and a store can print a count for a hole, a mini, a stick or a dozen. MEASURED ON THE REBUILT AND PUBLISHED BOARD, not on the reviewer's naive model: with holes and pods excluded (shipped today) the crown is Baker's "Bakery Fresh Glazed Yeast Donuts", 12 pk 2.5 oz, at $0.4167/each, and the cell keeps FOUR stores - Baker's $0.4167, Walmart $0.5033 ("Little Debbie Glazed Donut Sticks, 10.21 oz (6 count)"), Family Fare $0.5317 (the same Little Debbie sticks) and Sam's Club $0.6933 (3 oz bags of minis). So the runner-up is Walmart, not Family Fare as the plan first estimated, and TWO of the four surviving cells are donut STICKS rather than donuts. Which should Donuts mean? (A) keep per each and also exclude minis and sticks - the cell becomes Baker's only, since Walmart, Family Fare and Sam's all hold sticks or minis, and a one-store cell is close to no cell; (B) price Donuts per oz - every store's real donuts price (Baker's dozen $0.167/oz, Fareway Big Smile $0.29/oz, Aldi Bake Shop $0.30/oz) and holes, sticks and minis compete by weight instead of by an arbitrary printed count; (C) leave it as shipped, four cells with two of them sticks.
